text: Welcome to the teahouse. Climb the stair, drink the tea, look at the sea.

choices.text: Something stirred in me in that last fight. Like a current.
Bao says he cooks with his feet.

text: A current. Yes. Sailors call it Edy: the water turning back on itself behind a rock, round and round, never still and never gone.
Everyone has some. In most it sleeps. A hard fight wakes it, and then it wants to go somewhere.
It doesn't go the same way in everyone. Some are still water, some are fire, some are a storm. Before you spend it, you should know which you are.
Sit. Drink. Answer me honestly, and quickly. The first answer is the true one.
There. Now it knows where to go. Spend it as you earn it: the Captain's page will show you the paths.
And drink your tea. It's getting cold.
Edy is the current in you. Spend it on the paths: Iron Will, Sense, Tide, Tempo, Fury, Bond, and the one that rules the rest.
Your kind of Edy colours all of it, and leans you a little toward one way of fighting. If you ever feel you were read wrong, there's a reader on the capital's terrace. She charges like a duchess.
Bao? He came to me with a ladle in each hand and a temper like a stove. I gave him a kitchen and he gave the kitchen legs.
He's out front. If it's kicking you want, he's your man. Mind the teacups.
Tea from the far east, by way of Ysolde's junk and a great deal of arguing.
The keeper takes her lunch here every day and pays every other day. It evens out at the shrine.

bye.text: The sea's always there. So's the tea.
